title: Vector time and causal isomorphism
summary: Update vector clocks, compare timestamps componentwise, and use incomparability to detect concurrency.
objectives: Apply vector send and receive rules

sections.title: Per-process causal memory
sections.body: A vector clock stores one logical component per process. A process increments its own component before a local or send event and takes componentwise maxima before delivering a message.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: Vector updates are the main calculation depth of the supplied lecture: every component has a role, and receive order matters.

reference.sourceId: L. Lamport, Time, Clocks, and the Ordering of Events in a Distributed System

sections.title: Compare, do not sort
sections.body: One vector is less than another only when every component is no larger and at least one is smaller. If each vector is larger in a different component, the timestamps are incomparable and the events are concurrent.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: The vector comparison is a high-value distinction from scalar clocks: it can recover the causal partial order rather than inventing a total order.

reference.sourceId: L. Lamport, Time, Clocks, and the Ordering of Events in a Distributed System

examples.title: Componentwise comparison
steps: Check that at least one component is strictly smaller for a strict relation.
If each vector wins somewhere, report concurrency.
examples.answer: Do not compare vectors lexicographically; the relation is componentwise.

contrastDrills.explanation: Each vector is larger in one component, so neither dominates the other.
contrastDrills.misconception: Name the ordering, time, or communication boundary before choosing.

math.explanation: Before a local or send event, process i increments its own vector component. On receive, it first takes componentwise maxima and then performs the same local update.

symbols.meaning: vector timestamp held by process i

math.name: Vector-clock local update
math.purpose: Use it to record the local process's causal progress before a local or send event.

math.latex: vt_1<vt_2\ \Longleftrightarrow\ (\forall k,\ vt_1[k]\le vt_2[k])\land(\exists k,\ vt_1[k]<vt_2[k])
math.explanation: Strict vector order requires every component to be no larger and at least one component to be strictly smaller. If each vector exceeds the other somewhere, they are incomparable.
math.name: Vector-clock comparison
math.purpose: Use it to test componentwise causal order and detect concurrency when neither vector dominates.

criticalQuestions.prompt: Why is lexicographic sorting invalid for vector timestamps?
criticalQuestions.angle: A lexicographic rule can invent order when different processes have advanced independently.
criticalQuestions.modelAnswer: Causal comparison is componentwise. A vector can be larger in one component and smaller in another, which means concurrency rather than a total order.

criticalQuestions.prompt: What does the vector dimension represent?
criticalQuestions.angle: Connect one component to one process's causal progress.
criticalQuestions.modelAnswer: The vector has one component per process, so its size and message overhead grow with the number of processes.
